- [PREFERENCE] User loves classical music.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Giovanni Pierluigi da Palestrina (1525-1594) was a prolific composer of sacred music, known for his unique style of vocal polyphony emphasizing clarity and simplicity of texture.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Johann Sebastian Bach (1685-1750) was known for his intricate counterpoint and harmonic genius, particularly in keyboard music, especially the fugue.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart (1756-1791) composed over 600 works, known for their lyricism, elegance, and emotional depth.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Ludwig van Beethoven (1770-1827) marked a significant transition from the Classical to the Romantic period, known for emotional intensity and technical innovation.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Recommended work by Palestrina: Missa Papae Marcelli (Pope Marcellus Mass) - known for its purity and serenity of sound.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Recommended work by Bach: Brandenburg Concertos - showcases mastery of counterpoint and instrumental music.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Recommended work by Mozart: Eine kleine Nachtmusik (A Little Night Music) - known for its charm, grace, and elegant simplicity.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Recommended work by Beethoven: Symphony No. 9 - features a choral setting of "Ode to Joy" and is considered one of the greatest works in the Western musical canon.
